Sports.title: Mircea Lucescu, former Romania football captain and coach, dies aged 80
Sports.content:
Mircea Lucescu, the Romanian football great who was a serial trophy winner as a player and a coach, has died aged 80.

Lucescu’s death was confirmed by Bucharest university emergency hospital on Tuesday. He had been taken to hospital after reportedly having a heart attack on Friday morning.

“Mr Mircea Lucescu was one of the most successful Romanian football coaches and players, the first to qualify the national team for a European Championship, in 1984,” the hospital said in a statement. “Entire generations of Romanians grew up with his image in their hearts, as a national symbol.”

Lucescu had a lengthy coaching career and was in his second spell with the Romanian national team until stepping down last Thursday after falling ill during training. Three days earlier, Romania had missed out on qualification to the 2026 World Cup after losing 1-0 to Turkey in a playoff.

As a player, Lucescu won 64 caps and captained his country at the 1970 World Cup. His first stint as Romania manager began in 1981, and he led the team to the 1984 Euros after topping a qualifying group featuring Italy, Sweden and Czechoslovakia.

View image in fullscreen Mircea Lucescu (left) holds the Uefa Cup with the Shakhtar Donetsk owner, Rinat Akhmetov, after their victory over Werder Bremen in the 2009 final. Photograph: Carl Recine/Action Images/Reuters

During a well-travelled club coaching career, Lucescu managed teams across Europe, winning multiple titles. He won the Uefa Super Cup with Galatasaray in 2000, adding the Turkish title in 2001-02, and then winning the league with rivals Besiktas the following year.

In May 2004, Lucescu joined Ukrainian side Shakhar Donetsk and won eight titles in his 12-year tenure, plus the Uefa Cup in 2009. He went on to manage Zenit Saint Petersburg, Dynamo Kyiv and the Turkish national team, before returning to coach Romania after a 38-year gap to try and qualify for the World Cup.

“Thank you for everything, Mister. Your name is forever written into the history of world football,” Shakhtar posted on X. Galatasaray wrote in their tribute: “We extend our deepest condolences to Mircea Lucescu’s family, loved ones, and the football community. We will never forget you.”

Lucescu also coached Pisa, Brescia, Reggiana and Inter in Italy, winning Serie B with Brescia in 1991-92. He is fondly remembered by fans for his “Brescia Romeno” side, featuring four Romanian players, including Gheorghe Hagi.

Lucescu spoke to the Guardian in March this year, as he prepared his side for their playoff semi-final against Turkey while facing his own health issues. “I’m not in my best shape so I would have stepped away if there was another option available,” he said. “But I insist: I can’t leave like a coward. We must believe in our chance to qualify.”

“I felt it was my duty to take charge of the team,” he added. “It was my duty for everything that Romanian football has ever given to me. I was indebted. It was never about money, never about another medal. I have enough trophies.”

Sports.title: Arne Slot backs his Liverpool side to go ‘toe-to-toe’ with PSG in Champions League
Sports.content:
Arne Slot has warned Liverpool will suffer another emphatic defeat should they switch off against Paris Saint-Germain in their Champions League quarter-final first leg on Wednesday evening but believes his toiling team can save their season by going “toe-to-toe” with the European champions.

The pressure on Liverpool and their head coach has intensified following Saturday’s 4-0 capitulation against Manchester City in the quarter-final of the FA Cup. Florian Wirtz disagreed with the captain Virgil van Dijk’s damning assessment that Liverpool “gave up” at the Etihad Stadium, but both the £116m playmaker and Slot admitted there can be no repeat of that performance at Parc des Princes.

Slot, who will have Alexander Isak on the bench after four months out injured, claimed Luis Enrique’s team have improved since winning PSG’s first Champions League title last season and will punish any lapses from Liverpool. He challenged his players to “stand up again” and respond to the City embarrassment immediately.

“It’s not the first time we have 15-20 minutes in a game where we don’t play our best football and it is not the first time we immediately get punished by a goal, sometimes one or two,” Slot said of Saturday’s collapse. “This time it was four, the only four chances we gave up by the way. But the first 35 minutes gives me a lot of confidence that we can go toe-to-toe with teams [like City] and PSG who, for me, are the hardest to play against in open play. I have to say it like that, because of their quality and the way they are managed.

“But I can tell you that if we have the 20 minutes we had at City here, we will again concede four goals because these PSG players know how to act if we are having a 20-minute period like that. So it is a challenge for us to be from the first to the last second at the level we were at in the first 35 minutes. If not, it is going to be a really hard night, like it was on Saturday. Last year [in the Champions League last 16] we completely deserved to lose 4-0 here or maybe more, but that is the beauty of football that we scored a goal in the 85th minute and it was almost like this was a robbery.”

View image in fullscreen Alexander Isak is expected to be named among Liverpool’s substitutes after four months out. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

Slot claimed he had no issue with Van Dijk’s analysis of the City defeat: “It was good that the captain has a strong and firm reaction after a game like that. We have to have a strong and firm reaction too.” That sentiment was not shared by Wirtz, however, who claimed to be unaware of Van Dijk’s comment about the team giving up at a certain point against City and in disagreement with it.

“I didn’t know about this, that he said this, but I think I would not agree directly because we still tried to create chances to turn the game around,” said the Germany international. “Of course when the game gets longer and you are 3-0 back or something in the 80th minute [it was 4-0 after 57 minutes] then mentally it is difficult to go and go. At 3-0 and 4-0 we still had a few chances but this is not our standards that we lose 4-0 against City.

“We still believe in ourselves. We have a good group with good characters and great players, also a good manager who tries to prepare us good for the game. The second game at home is maybe an advantage so we try to do our best and come with a good result to Anfield.”

Liverpool have won only once in five matches, at home to Galatasaray in the last-16 second leg at Anfield, and the manner of the FA Cup defeat – with four goals conceded in 18 minutes and fans streaming for the exits after 57 minutes – invited the question of whether the team is still playing for Slot. “Yes of course we are believing in the manager,” replied Wirtz.

“The team should believe in the manager because they won the league last season. We had a lot of good games this season. We wanted it to be better but we still have things to play for. Everything I can see is that we believe in the manager and we will give our best on the pitch tomorrow.”

Both Wirtz and Slot made frequent mentions of keeping the tie alive for next week’s second leg at Anfield and the head coach could make changes – in personnel and formation – in response to the City defeat. But what can pull Liverpool out of their slump, Slot maintained, is character. “This club has always shown that they stand up again in tough moments,” he said. “We’ve had a lot of tough moments this season and stood up a few times, but then fallen down again. So we have to show that mentality again of just keep going and picking yourself up after a disappointment.

“It is easier said than done but this group has shown many times it can come back after setbacks. And this club has done it many, many times. Apart from the quality my team has – and PSG has too – my team has shown many times in big games, with the exception of twice at the Etihad, that we can compete with the best teams in Europe.”

Sports.title: Daniil Medvedev smashes racket SEVEN times in Monte Carlo meltdown as tennis' tantrum tyrant endures worst loss of his career
Sports.content:
Daniil Medvedev smashed his racket seven times in an on-court meltdown as he suffered a 6-0, 6-0 defeat for the first time in his career.

The former world No.1 was handed a tough start to his clay court season at the Monte Carlo Masters after being drawn against Italy's Matteo Berrettini.

Medvedev, who has typically struggled on the surface during his career, had begun positively by forcing break points in the opening game but Berrettini ultimately held serve.

The match quickly became a one-sided contest with Berrettini winning the first set 6-0 in just 25 minutes.

Medvedev's frustrations boiled over in the early stages of the second set, as Berrettini broke serve once again to take a 2-0 advantage.

In response, Medvedev smashed his racket on the court and was then seen throwing it in anger.

Medvedev definitely still hating playing on clay pic.twitter.com/iklmIxaIkA — Sam (@LoverLondonGirl) April 8, 2026

Daniil Medvedev smashed his racket seven times in an on-court meltdown in Monte Carlo

Medvedev's frustations boiled over as he suffered a 6-0, 6-0 defeat for the first time in his career

Medvedev threw the racket a further four times, with the crowd cheering each one, before eventually smashing it for a seventh and final time near his player's bench. The meltdown lasted 40 seconds.

'It had been coming everybody,' the Sky Sports commentator commented in response to the outburst, before quipping 'Yeah, I think that's unusable' as Medvedev was seen placing the remains of the racket into a courtside bin.

Medvedev, who was given a warning for unsportsmanlike conduct by the umpire, would ultimately go on to suffer the worst defeat of his career as Berrettini completed a 6-0, 6-0 victory.

Speaking on Sky Sports, former British star Jamie Murray admitted he was shocked by the incident and Medvedev's display.

'It is shocking, it shouldn't happen... It did,' Murray said.

'[But] I am not sure how much effect that will have on him going forward.

'I think he will be pretty embarrassed walking into the locker room and will probably be wanting to get off site pretty quickly.

'He played so well in Indian Wells as well. He talks about clay not being his favourite surface and the difficulties he has on it but he won in Rome. If you can win in Rome, you can play on clay.

Medvedev has been in impressive form so far in 2026 but endured a nightmare start to the clay season

'It was a big surprise to see him go down with two eggs, but fair play to Berrettini, that's not an easy thing to do.'

Medvedev has a long history of on-court outbursts, with one of the most notable coming at the US Open last August when he was involved in a heated exchange with an umpire, contributing to a six-minute delay to his match.

The meltdown occurred as he endured a nightmare string of results at Grand Slams, winning just one match across tennis' four most prestigious events.

A coaching change, however, saw Medvedev's form rebound in the final months of 2025 and his upward trajectory has continued so far this season, leading to him returning to the world's top 10.

Medvedev has won titles in Brisbane and Dubai this year, while he beat world No.1 Carlos Alcaraz en route to reaching the final of Indian Wells, where he lost to Jannik Sinner in a closely fought contest.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury breaks silence on explosive fall-out with dad John after retirement U-turn left their relationship 'destroyed completely' - as Tommy Fury insists the 'entire family' don't want him to fight again
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury breaks silence on explosive fall-out with dad John after retirement U-turn left their relationship 'destroyed completely' - as Tommy Fury insists the 'entire family' don't want him to fight again

Tyson Fury has shared his side of the story as to why his relationship with father John has broken down, revealing that his return to boxing once more is the catalyst for their falling out.

In an exclusive interview with Daily Mail Sport, Fury Sr said their relationship is 'destroyed completely'.

At the start of the year, Fury Jr announced that he is making his latest comeback to the sport with a heavyweight bout against Arslanbek Makhmudov on April 11.

It will be Fury's first fight since December 2024 when he was beaten for a second time by rival Oleksandr Usyk.

And as he goes through the preparations of fight week, the Gypsy King has revealed that his dad has wanted him to retire from boxing ever since he beat Deontay Wilder in the second part of their trilogy in February 2020.

'He's not happy. He wanted me to retire in 2020 after I beat Deontay Wilder,' he told Good Morning Britain on Wednesday.

Tyson Fury has revealed his version as to why he has fallen out with his father John

Fury pictured with John ahead of his February press conference with Arslanbek Makhmudov

Speaking on Good Morning Britain, Fury said his dad hasn't wanted him to box since 2020

'He's just not happy, he does not want me to box. I suppose any parent wouldn't want their kid to continue to do something they've done from being a little kid all the way to being an adult at the end of their sporting age.

'I think he's concerned. When it's your kids, when it's your close relatives or whatever, I think you feel very concerned for the individual.

'He's got his opinions and he doesn't want me to do it – he never has wanted me to do it for the past six years.

'At the end of the day, every man must bear his own cross and it's my destiny to do.'

Asked if there is any chance of his dad attending this weekend's bout at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the 37-year-old didn't have much hope.

'He might do, he might do, he might do. But he didn't come to the Usyk II fight so I'm not holding my breath,' he continued.

'My dad will do what my dad will do, he's his own man and there's nothing I can do about it. If he turns up, great and if he doesn't, also great.'

Fury's younger brother Tommy echoed John's sentiments in an interview with Bloody Elbow this week, revealing that nobody in the boxing clan wants the Gypsy King to fight again.

'I think if you asked any one of his family do we want to see him keeping boxing the answer would have been an all around 'no'. That's all the way around the board because we care about his health.

'Obviously you guys are fight fans you love to see him in the ring because he brings that entertainment. But we think of his health and everything like that so listen, he's decided to keep fighting, it's Tyson who is a fighting man who loves to do so. But I guess time will tell and I think he definitely still has it in him because he wouldn't be getting in that ring if he knew he didn't.'

Speaking to Daily Mail Sport last month, courtesy of Playbook Boxing, Fury Sr was emotional when describing the separation with his son.

'My relationship with Tyson is destroyed. Boxing destroyed it completely. I'll say it on camera: I've never taken £10 off him in my life and I never will.

'I don't want Tyson's money and I don't need Tyson's money. Whatever he's got, good luck to him. But, don't forget who built his story when he was a kid. He didn't build it himself, did he? Me, his father.

'I was 30 seconds away from asking for a break there. I haven't really expressed these emotions before but they're strong and they're there.

'I think he's past his best. I'm a no-filter kind of guy - I say it how I see it. I love him, but there are too many people patting him on the back and telling him things that aren't true, building him up like he's invincible. He's not and he hasn't been for a while.

'Tyson has been gone since the Deontay Wilder fights, they finished him. Wilder completely done him. He's not got a leg underneath him. He's took a lot away from Tyson. Makhmudov is a problem for Tyson. I am the first one to say it.

Speaking last month John said his relationship with his son is 'destroyed completely'

'Listen, I understand now that Tyson is testing himself. But, I can tell you now, his legs aren't there anymore. I understand the only way he will believe that and see that is when the first bell rings.

'Tyson was a formidable man, but when you fight one of the hardest punchers in boxing history three times, it takes something out of you that you never get back. You can't refill that tank to what it once was. And every shot he took matters.

'Don't forget, in the last fight he went down four times - huge, heavy punches. He fought his heart out, went to the absolute limit, and gave everything he had to get that knockout. But when he got it, he had nothing left afterwards.



'He laid it all on the line. He even said himself - after everything - that he was prepared to die in there if it came to it. That's the kind of mentality he had: willing to risk everything in the ring.'

Sports.title: Former Champions League manager dies less than two weeks after leading his country in World Cup play-off
Sports.content:
Former Champions League manager dies less than two weeks after leading his country in World Cup play-off

Romanian football has been rocked by the death of recent men's national team manager Mircea Lucescu, less than a fortnight after he attempted to guide them to this summer's World Cup.

Lucescu's death at the age of 80 at the Bucharest University Emergency Hospital was announced by the Romanian Football Federation (FRF) on Tuesday.

He was taken to hospital late last month after falling ill during a meeting before a training session with Romania ahead of a friendly in Slovakia on March 31.

It has been reported that he suffered a heart attack on the morning of Good Friday too.

Lucescu had a lengthy coaching career and was in his second spell with the Romanian national team until stepping down on April 2 due to his health.

The week before on March 26, Lucescu was unable to guide Romania past Turkey in their World Cup play-off semi-final - as the visitors lost 1-0 in Istanbul.

Romanian football icon Mircea Lucescu has died at the age of 80, it was announced on Tuesday

Less than a fortnight ago, Lucescu took charge of Romania's World Cup play-off loss to Turkey

In a statement, the FRF - who have suspended the search for Lucescu's replacement for an indefinite period - paid tribute to such a pivotal character in Romanian football.

'It is a black day for Romania and for world football. A man who lived through and for football in every second of his existence has left us,' they said.

'He was a man who loved this sport more than anything in life, and his impact on our football is immeasurable.'

The Bucharest University Emergency Hospital also paid their respects, stating: 'Mr Mircea Lucescu was one of the most successful Romanian football coaches and players, the first to qualify the Romanian national team for a European Championship, in 1984.

'Entire generations of Romanians grew up with his image in their hearts, as a national symbol.'

Known for his tactical discipline and talent development, Lucescu leaves a legacy as one of the most successful coaches in European club football in terms of number of trophies won.

His most prominent period of success came during a 12-year tenure at Shakhtar Donetsk, where he led the side to eight Ukrainian league titles and the 2009 UEFA Cup. He also guided the club to the Champions League quarter-finals in 2010-11 - the furthest they have ever progressed in the competition.

Ex-Premier League duo Fernandinho and Henrikh Mkhitaryan, who both played for him at Shakhtar, are among Lucescu's former players to pay tribute to him on social media.

View this post on Instagram

View this post on Instagram

Lucescu also secured championships in Turkey with rivals Galatasaray and Besiktas, and spent time in Italy with Inter Milan and Brescia.

A former national team captain who led Romania to Euro 1984 as a young coach, Lucescu is widely credited with modernising the country's football infrastructure.

During his playing days as a winger he won seven league titles and the Romanian Cup for Dinamo Bucharest. He established himself as one of the country's most decorated figures, captaining Romania at the 1970 World Cup and winning 64 caps over more than a decade.

'European and world football have lost an exceptional figure whose influence, stature and legacy will endure for generations to come,' said UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin.

'Mircea Lucescu was one of the game's true originals - a man of rare football intellect, remarkable dignity and passion, whose contribution to the sport is difficult to measure in words alone.



'His presence shaped teams, inspired players and colleagues, and left a lasting imprint on football far beyond the touchline.'

Sports.title: Lando Norris reunites with model girlfriend Magui Corceiro as they appear to put split rumours to bed at Arsenal's Champions League victory
Sports.content:
Formula One world champion Lando Norris appears to have reunited with his girlfriend Magui Corceiro after the pair were seen together watching a Champions League game on Tuesday.

Norris and Corceiro were pictured alongside each other in the stands as Arsenal beat Sporting Lisbon 1-0 at the Jose Alvalade Stadium.

Portuguese newspaper A Bola reported that Norris and Corceiro had travelled to Lisbon together on a private jet ahead of the match.

They were joined by singer April Ivy, who previously dated Ruben Dias.

Norris has dated Corceiro on-and-off since 2023 and she was by his side during the emotional title-winning scenes in Abu Dhabi last year.

Norris and Corceiro, who used to go out with footballer Joao Felix, previously broke up in 2024 before reconciling.

Lando Norris was spotted alongside Magui Corceiro at Sporting Lisbon's Champions League match with Arsenal

Norris set tongues wagging in February when he appeared to tell Carlos Sainz he was 'a single man'

Corceiro was also joined by singer April Ivy, right, in the stands at the match

Rumours emerged back in February that the couple had gone their separate ways again.

Speculation ramped up after a video of Norris appeared to show him telling Carlos Sainz Jr he is a 'single man'.

In a TikTok clip, Williams driver Sainz asked: 'Are you and Magui good?'

Norris responds with 'No', before appearing to say he is 'a single man', though the audio quality was poor.

F1 insider Kym Illman then shared a video to Instagram, telling his 900,000 followers that rumours of a split between the pair were 'definitely true'.

'Lando Norris was in fine form this morning, looking good,' Illman said at the Bahrain Grand Prix.

'You may read this tomorrow... but he has broken up with his girlfriend Magui. You might have already heard rumours but it is definitely true.'

Norris and Corceiro have publicly shared messages between each other.

A teary Corceiro was one of the first to congratulate Norris when he was crowned world champion in December

Portuguese model Corceiro has been in an on-and-off relationship with Norris since 2023

Corceiro had commented on this Instagram photo of Norris recently

Norris uploaded photos from his off-season break in the snow during the festive period - with the photo dump captioned: 'Left this draft in the freezer'.

In the first picture in the sequence, Norris can be seen wrapped up warmly, while wearing some red tartan bottoms.

And that photo caught the eye of Corceiro who commented: 'Nice pjs, u [sic] welcome.'

Back in December, Corceiro broke down in tears after watching Norris triumph to take the world championship.

In the week that followed, the model and actress gave an interview with TV Guia, saying: 'There's no rule for going public,' she said. 'I thought it (the kiss in Abu Dhabi) made sense. I'm very happy, he's very happy, and that's what matters.

'At that moment I forgot the cameras were there. It was such an important moment that I didn't even remember that.'

Corceiro was in attendance for the post-victory celebrations along with his parents Adam and Cisca, his brother Oliver and McLaren team.

It's understood the group partied through the night until 6am on Monday, racking up a bill worth around £100,000 across the hotel bars they visited.

The stars' relationship has been one of the more high profile on the Formula One grid

Corceiro hails from Santarem in Portugal and has amassed a colossal social media following including 800,000 fans on TikTok.

As an actress, she has appeared in Portuguese television dramas and is regularly featured in campaigns, including stints for Intimissimi and Alo Yoga.

Corceiro was a contestant in the country's version of Dancing with the Stars back in 2020.

She also co-founded the eco-conscious swimwear brand Missus and has graced the pages of Vogue Portugal.

Sports.title: Tottenham confirm Roberto De Zerbi backroom staff with just TWO of Italian's key team joining as club battles to avoid relegation
Sports.content:
Tottenham confirm Roberto De Zerbi backroom staff with just TWO of Italian's key team joining as club battles to avoid relegation

Roberto De Zerbi will attempt to keep Tottenham in the Premier League without several of his usual coaching team.

Only two of De Zerbi’s seven key staff will join him at Spurs for the last seven games of this season.

Those two are fitness coach Marcattilio Marcattilii, who has worked with him for more 10 years since they were together at Foggia, and senior development phase coach Marcello Quinto, a coach who joined him at Brighton.

Others including Andrea Maldera, who was his assistant manager at Brighton and Marseille, and Enrico Venturelli, a familiar figure during their time at Brighton where his roles included helping De Zerbi with translation, will not join him at Spurs for the rest of this season.

Bruno Saltor, who joined Spurs to assist interim boss Igor Tudor in February, will continue as an assistant coach.

Former Brighton defender Saltor left the Amex Stadium before De Zerbi’s arrival and worked with Graham Potter at Chelsea and West Ham.

New Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi has added just two coaches to his backroom staff

Marcattilio Marcattili and Marcello Quinto have joined as first team fitness coach and senior professional development phase coach, respectively

De Zerbi has been tasked with keeping relegation-threatened Tottenham in the Premier League

Goalkeeping coach Fabian Otte, set-piece coach Andreas Georgson and individual development coach Cameroon Campbell, all appointed last summer under Thomas Frank, will continue in their roles along with Stuart Lewis and Dean Brill.



De Zerbi, who signed a five-year contract with no relegation escape, will take charge of his first Spurs game at Sunderland on Sunday.

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard names the £65.5m former Liverpool star he wants BACK at Anfield - and reveals his ideal Mo Salah replacement
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard names the £65.5m former Liverpool star he wants BACK at Anfield - and reveals his ideal Mo Salah replacement

Former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard has admitted he 'misses' Luis Diaz at Anfield and would love to see the Bayern Munich forward back at the club.

Diaz left the Reds in the summer after three years of service, departing for £65.5million to join the German champions after he and the Premier League side failed to agree terms on a new contract.

He has had a positive first season in the Bundesliga, picking up 40 goal involvements in just 39 games and forming a lethal front three with Harry Kane and Michael Olise. He also put his side 1-0 up in the first leg of their Champions League quarter-final clash with Real Madrid on Tuesday night.

Liverpool, meanwhile, have struggled this season, failing to replace Diaz on the left of their attack under Arne Slot.

And Gerrard wants him back. Speaking on TNT Sports before Bayern's clash with Real Madrid, he said: 'I wouldn't mind Diaz back. I'm missing him, I'm missing him.'

Gerrard also gave his thought on Olise, who has been linked with a potential move to Liverpool as a replacement for Mohamed Salah, who is leaving this summer.

Steven Gerrard has admitted he misses Luis Diaz (right) at Liverpool and would love to see him return to Anfield

Gerrard (left) also picked out Michael Olise (right) as a replacement for Mohamed Salah in the summer transfer window

The Frenchman is in the form of his life with the German club as part of that front three, and has picked up 44 goal involvements in 40 games this season, with 16 goals himself.

With a contract until 2029, the 24-year-old would cost a pretty penny, but Gerrard would be keen to see Liverpool cough up.

'When you are a full back up against a winger, they normally have a weak side and you show them one way or another,' Gerrard said. 'The problem with him is he can go both ways - his right foot is just as strong as his left.

'You see some of the assists he gets. If you leave him in 1-v-1 situations, you are in trouble.'

When asked if he would take Olise at Liverpool, he said: 'All day long. But the problem is, why would he leave Bayern? A big club challenging for the big honours and they are probably the strongest Bayern team we have seen for a while.

'He is about to take the World Cup by storm. He looks like a really happy kid - settled, to me - and I don't think he's going anywhere. But would I take him at Liverpool? Yes, I would love him.'

Reports in Germany suggest Liverpool are willing to put £173million on the table to sign the former Crystal Palace star, with Spanish side Real Madrid ready to bid £143m to bolster their attack. Bayern, though, insist their star isn't going anywhere.

'We're not even considering that,' Bayern sporting director Max Eberl told German publication BILD. 'He's an FC Bayern player and has all the opportunities here that top players could wish for.'



CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen, meanwhile, added: 'No matter which club tries to lure him away, anyone who plays for FC Bayern knows what they have at FC Bayern.'

Sports.title: From the star who has been without a club since 2024 to the midfielder who retired at 28 to become a travel agent! The fates of the 14 players given Man United debuts by Louis van Gaal
Sports.content:
Next month marks 10 years since Louis van Gaal was brutally sacked as Manchester United manager despite guiding the club to FA Cup glory.

The Dutchman brought the Red Devils their first trophy in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era with a 2-1 victory over Crystal Palace after extra-time at Wembley.

Van Gaal, a big believer in bringing young players through, promoted 14 youngsters to the first team during his two-year spell at Old Trafford.

Earlier this month, one of those youngsters ended his two-year exile from the game by signing for second-tier United States club New Mexico United.

But what has become of the other 13 stars? Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the very different paths that Van Gaal's proteges have taken following their United debuts.

Louis van Gaal (right) handed 14 Man United youth or reserve players their first-team debuts

Tyler Blackett

Manchester United debut: 2-1 defeat vs Swansea (Premier League), August 2014

Let's begin with the star who has found a new club in the United States. Tyler Blackett made his Manchester United debut in Van Gaal's first competitive game in charge.

The Dutchman's preference for left-footed defenders saw Blackett make 12 appearances under him in the 2014-15 campaign. That is as good as it got though for Blackett at United, who left the club in August 2016 to sign with Reading.

Now 32, he's just joined New Mexico United in the USL Championship - the second division of American football after MLS. His move comes two years after he was released upon the expiration of his contract by Championship side Rotherham United following their relegation to League One.

Tyler Blackett made 12 appearances for Man United during Van Gaal's first season in 2014-15

Cameron Borthwick-Jackson

Manchester United debut: 2-0 win vs West Brom (Premier League), November 2015

Another left-footed defender, and just like Blackett, Cameron Borthwick-Jackson made all of his appearances for United in one season under Van Gaal. He played 11 times for the club in all competitions after making his debut in the 2015-16 season. Capitalising on an injury period among more senior players, Borthwick-Jackson impressed before injuries hampered his own playing time.

He signed a four-year contract at Old Trafford a week after Jose Mourinho replaced Van Gaal but he never made a first-team appearance under the Portuguese and eventually joined Oldham Athletic on a free transfer in 2020.

Now 29, he joined Macclesfield in January on a short-term deal until the end of the season and came on as a second-half substitute in their famous FA Cup third-round win over Palace this season.

Cameron Borthwick-Jackson (right) was emotional after Macclesfield's win vs Crystal Palace

Timothy Fosu-Mensah

Manchester United debut: 3-2 win vs Arsenal (Premier League), February 2016

Timothy Fosu-Mensah was tipped for a promising career at Old Trafford but could ultimately never nail down a regular position as he struggled with fitness issues.

The Dutchman made 10 appearances in his debut 2015-16 season for United and 11 in the next, before spending the next two campaigns on loan at Crystal Palace and Fulham in the Premier League.

However, his spell at Fulham was cut short when he suffered a knee ligament injury. After returning to action in the Covid-hit 2019-20 campaign, he would only feature nine more times for United before leaving in January 2021.

His time at Bayer Leverkusen was also injury-ridden, making only 30 appearances during his time there before being released at the end of 2023-24 term.

Fosu-Mensah has been a free agent since, as he looks to prove his fitness, but was training with Palace's Under 21s last month.

Timothy Fosu-Mensah (lefr) has been a free agent since being released by Bayer Leverkusen in 2024

Reece James

Manchester United debut: 4-0 defeat at MK Dons (League Cup), August 2014

No, not the Chelsea captain, but he is a full back. James made his only United appearance in that abysmal League Cup thrashing at MK Dons - in a game that sparked the end of many players' careers with United.

He spent the rest of that season out on loan at Rotherham and Huddersfield Town, before joining Wigan Athletic in July 2015.

The full back has spent the majority of his career in the Championship and League One, and is back with The Millers - although they are mired in a relegation battle at present.

Reece James is looking to help Rotherham avoid relegation from League One this season

Saidy Janko

Manchester United debut: 4-0 defeat at MK Dons (League Cup), August 2014

Like James, Saidy Janko started that shocking loss in Milton Keynes and like his fellow full-back never played for United again. Hooked at half-time, he was then sent on loan to Bolton for the remainder of the season in February 2015.

He joined Celtic on a four-year contract that summer and has signed for the likes of Saint-Etienne, Porto, Nottingham Forest (loan) and Real Valladolid since. Now on the books of Swiss side Young Boys.

Saidy Janko (centre left) is currently playing for Swiss side Young Boys

Jesse Lingard

Manchester United debut: 2-1 defeat vs Swansea (Premier League), August 2014

One of the standout and most successful names on this list, Jesse Lingard started in Van Gaal's first game - albeit in the unfamiliar role of right wing-back. However, his debut was curtailed after 24 minutes due to injury in what would be his only club outing that term as he joined Derby County on loan until the end of the season in February 2015.

He made an impact for United in Van Gaal's second and final campaign though, featuring 40 times in all competitions and scoring the winning goal in the FA Cup final against Palace.

Lingard would go on to play 232 times in total for the club, scoring 35 times, before leaving on a free transfer at the end of the 2021-22 season. He left Old Trafford winning three major honours: the FA Cup (2015-16), League Cup (2016-17) and Europa League (2016-17). He became an England international during that time too - earning 32 caps and scoring six goals.

His last season at United included a successful loan spell at West Ham but the midfielder decided to join Nottingham Forest on a free that summer. Lingard has travelled the world since his spell at the City Ground, spending two years at FC Seoul in South Korea before joining Brazilian giants Corinthians on a one-year deal in March.

Jesse Lingard scored the winning goal in the 2015-16 FA Cup final to give Van Gaal silverware

Donald Love

Manchester United debut: 2-1 defeat at Sunderland (Premier League), February 2016

Donald Love made his Red Devils debut during the club's defensive injury crisis, with the club recalling him from his loan spell at Wigan Athletic as a result. He came on as a second-half substitute for Matteo Darmian in a 2-1 defeat by Sunderland, and was on the losing side five days later when he started during the 2-1 loss at Midtjylland in the Europa League.

He joined the Black Cats in a combined double transfer with Paddy McNair worth £5.5million in August 2016. He was released three years later and has remained playing in the EFL since. The former Scotland U21 international is now at Accrington Stanley in League Two.

Former Scotland Under-21 international Donald Love is now playing for Accrington Stanley

Paddy McNair

Manchester United debut: 2-1 win vs West Ham (Premier League), September 2014

Paddy McNair was an unused substitute in the defeat at MK Dons but made his debut a month later in a 2-1 win over West Ham, starting at centre back due to the club's injuries. He made 18 appearances in total that season, with his first four all ending in victory. He featured nine times in Van Gaal's second season before joining Sunderland with Love.

The 30-year-old has become a mainstay in the Northern Ireland set-up, playing 81 times for his country. He has spent the majority of his career in the Championship and is now at Hull City - joining in January.

Paddy McNair (right) has become a key part in the Northern Ireland XI since leaving United

Andreas Pereira

Manchester United debut: 4-0 defeat at MK Dons (League Cup), August 2014

Not as fruitful a career as Lingard's, Andreas Pereira did establish himself as a Premier League midfielder though. The Brazilian came on at half-time for Janko in that galling loss to MK Dons for his United debut, but - unlike many others - that wasn't the end of his Old Trafford career. He only made one appearance in 2014-15 and then 11 in 2015-16 before spending time out on loan in Spain for the next two campaigns (Granada - 2016-17 and Valencia - 2017-18).

Pereira returned to the United fold across 2018-19 and 2019-20, making 62 appearances in that period. However, he then spent the next couple of years on loan again at Lazio (2020-21) and Flamengo (2021 and 2022) before signing for Fulham in a £10m transfer.

His three successful years at Craven Cottage ended with a surprise return to Brazil. He's now at Palmeiras in his homeland after leaving Fulham in August 2025.

Andreas Pereira is playing in his homeland of Brazil - having joined Palmeiras in August 2025

Regan Poole

Manchester United debut: 5-1 win vs Midtjylland (Europa League), February 2016

Regan Poole's only appearance was a second-half substitute in stoppage time in a match that made the name of another Man United youngster - the club's 5-1 home win over Midtjylland. He was released by United at the end of the 2018-19 season but has since made a career for himself in the Football League.

The 27-year-old, who has one Wales cap to his name, currently plays for Portsmouth in the Championship.

Regan Poole (bottom) is currently playing for Portsmouth and has represented Wales once

Marcus Rashford

Manchester United debut: 5-1 win vs Midtjylland (Europa League), February 2016

The most successful name on this list, Marcus Rashford only made his debut against Midtjylland due to an injury to Anthony Martial in the warm-up and Will Keane having to pull out at the last minute. The then-18-year-old truly announced himself though, scoring twice in a 5-1 win. He followed that up days later with a brace and an assist as injury-hit United stunned Arsenal 3-2 in the Premier League. Just a few weeks later he would score the matchwinner in a 1-0 victory at Manchester City too.

His debut term ended with 18 appearances and eight goals and FA Cup glory, while also making his England debut and being part of their Euro 2016 squad.

The forward has scored 138 goals in 426 appearances during 10 seasons at United, winning two FA Cups (the other being 2023-24), two League Cups (2016-17 and 2022-23) and a Europa League (2016-17) for his major honours haul.

Despite the good times, there have been tough ones too with Rashford spending the second half of last season on loan at Aston Villa after falling out with former United boss Ruben Amorim. He's currently on a season-long loan at Barcelona - with the Spanish giants keen to make it a permanent deal in the future.

Marcus Rashford is currently on loan at Barcelona with he and the club hoping to make it a permanent transfer

Joe Riley

Manchester United debut: 3-0 win at Shrewsbury Town (FA Cup), February 2016

Making his Red Devils debut as a half-time substitute for Borthwick-Jackson, Joe Riley made his one and only start for the club a few days later in the Europa League at Midtjylland with Chris Smalling out injured.

He spent the next two seasons on loan in League One at Sheffield United and Bradford City before signing for the latter permanently on a two-year deal in May 2018. He now plays for Tamworth in the National League.

Joe Riley made two appearances for the Red Devils in 2015-16 and is now playing for Tamworth

Tom Thorpe

Manchester United debut: 2-1 win vs West Ham (Premier League), September 2014

The Manchester United academy graduate only played 111 seconds for the club - coming on as a late substitute for Angel di Maria against West Ham in September 2014. Tom Thorpe was released at the end of that 2014-15 season, joining Rotherham on a two-year deal.

Now 33, he has been without a club since leaving non-league outfit Stalybridge Celtic in November 2023.

Tom Thorpe made a brief cameo against West Ham and has been without a club since 2023

James Weir

Manchester United debut: 3-2 win vs Arsenal (Premier League), February 2016

James Weir's sole appearance for Manchester United was as second-half stoppage-time substitute in the win over Arsenal. That season he was an unused substitute a further seven times.

James Weir (left) came on briefly against Arsenal and is now retired, becoming a travel agent

He joined Hull City in August 2016, despite being offered a new deal at Old Trafford, but only made seven appearances in three years at the club - which included a loan spell at Wigan.

Weir would later join Bolton, but then spent the next part of his career abroad - playing in Slovakia, Hungary and back in Slovakia. In February 2024 he announced his retirement at the age of 28 due to injuries and turned his hand to becoming an independent travel agent for players, families and agents.

Sports.title: These are the three instructions Arne Slot must give his players if Liverpool are to beat PSG - and how Liam Rosenior's Chelsea gave him the starting points for shock success in Paris
Sports.content:
Before travelling to the Parc des Princes for their Champions League quarter-final with Paris Saint-Germain tonight, Liverpool’s analysts will have pored over what happened when Chelsea made the same trip last month.

Among their observations will be how Liam Rosenior adopted a brave approach, namely in the way he had his players seek to press the Parisians on their own patch.

Rosenior’s side did not go to Paris with a plan to sit back, to defend deep, to counter and pray.

They took the game to the reigning champions of Europe and while the scoreline — a 5-2 defeat in the last-16 first leg — would suggest this ended in disaster for Chelsea, it should not deter Liverpool from trying to do the same.

Arne Slot's side have had issues when pressing teams high this season, granted. Not least against Manchester City at the weekend, when City bypassed the Reds' midfield with ease. Liverpool's coaching staff also saw first-hand how dominant PSG's midfield can be at Anfield last March.

But those who watched Chelsea's first leg unfold can say they were arguably the better side until Filip Jorgensen’s mistake gifted PSG the goal for their 3-2 lead in the 74th minute. It was only then that it all unravelled for the visitors.

Liverpool looked badly out of sorts in their 4-0 defeat by Manchester City on Saturday, and they face another tough assignment away to Paris Saint-Germain tonight

Arne Slot knows better than anyone how dominant PSG's midfield can be, after his side lost to the Parisians in the last-16 last March

But Chelsea proved last month that you can have success in Paris by pressing PSG aggressively, with Enzo Fernandez scoring after the Blues won possession high up the pitch

Before then, Chelsea were in the tie, positioning themselves high up the pitch to try to secure turnovers and scoring twice through Malo Gusto and Enzo Fernandez. Both goals came seconds after the visitors forced PSG into giving up possession.

We know Liverpool are not the pressing monsters they were under Jurgen Klopp, but Slot should recognise that PSG can be vulnerable to a high press, and beatable.

PSG goalkeeper Matvei Safonov did not appear the most reliable versus Chelsea, and so Liverpool should be seeking to test him at the Parc des Princes themselves.

BEWARE THE PSG COUNTER

The risk with Chelsea’s approach was it gave one of the world’s most talented attacks, led by Ousmane Dembele, the opportunity to charge at them on the counter.

PSG’s second goal, for example, arrived 14 seconds after a shot by Cole Palmer was saved by Safonov at the other end. That move also involved Dembele twisting and turning Wesley Fofana, who did not cover himself in glory defensively.

Liverpool will have to be prepared for those situations if and when their players are positioned high and they lose possession. But Chelsea showed if you get at PSG and respond well when required, then you can have some joy amid a hostile atmosphere.

Slot’s side have been poor at defending counter-attacks this year. The pairing of Ibrahima Konate and Virgil van Dijk has been exploited too many times, while midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Alexis Mac Allister can be found wanting out of possession.

Ibrahima Konate and Virgil van Dijk have been exposed too many times this season - they will have to be at their best to deal with PSG's threat on the counter

Ryan Gravenberch will also have to up his game out of possession to deal with the likes of Vitinha

Their back four in the loss to City, which included Joe Gomez at right back, was lacking in pace. Jeremie Frimpong could be fit enough to start in Paris — but will he begin in the front three, as he has done in several European games this term?

In any case, Rosenior held no regrets over his high-risk approach in Paris.

When reporters pressed him on it a few days later at Chelsea's Cobham training ground, the Blues boss said: ‘I could play 5-4-1, sit back, kick them the ball back, not give them a counter-attack, they win 4-0. I’ve seen that in Ligue 1, I’ve seen that in the Champions League. I live and die off hindsight.’

DON’T BE NAIVE LIKE JORGENSEN

As mentioned, it all unravelled for Chelsea after 74 minutes when Jorgensen tried and failed to pass out from the back, which ended with him picking the ball out of his own goal.

When Chelsea beat PSG in the summer’s Club World Cup final, Enzo Maresca had his goalkeeper, Robert Sanchez, play long passes towards the wingers. That gave PSG little chance of robbing him of possession at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

But Rosenior saw something in Jorgensen’s passing ability in training, trusted him for that Champions League trip, and ultimately, his insistence on playing out of his box helped PSG.

With Alisson Becker injured, Liverpool will be using their own younger understudy Giorgi Mamardashvili in goal. He should not seek to play into PSG’s hands in the same way Jorgensen did. Even if under orders to pass from the back, he must assess the situation and adapt when needed.

Filip Jorgensen's naive passing out from the back cost Chelsea dearly in Paris last month

Robert Sanchez's pass map from Chelsea's Club World Cup triumph over PSG in July shows how his direct kicking effectively bypassed the Parisians' high press - Giorgi Mamardashvili must be similarly adaptable tonight

Mamardashvili, the big Georgian, is calm with the ball at his feet but he is not Alisson. See Brighton’s first goal two weeks ago: the goalkeeper was made to panic by the Seagulls' press and conceded a cheap throw-in which led to a goal.

Alisson has been known to go long at times but he does not have the same outlets any more. After a stellar year for Gravenberch, teams now target him and Mac Allister and shut off the pair as passing options.

Jorgensen was still trying to pass out of his box towards the end of that first leg, even after he had already allowed Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to score PSG’s third.

Chelsea’s vice-captain Fernandez threw the ball at his goalkeeper in anger at one stage for sticking to that strategy. Will Mamardashvili learn from his mistake tonight?

Sports.title: 'Rory McIlroy told me to f*** off during angry exchange – this is what he is really like'
Sports.content:
'Rory McIlroy told me to f*** off during angry exchange – this is what he is really like'

Masters champion Rory McIlroy's thoughts on a book being written about him have been revealed

View 3 Images Rory McIlroy made his feelings towards a writer perfectly clear (Image: Getty Images)

Rory McIlroy told an author writing a book about the Masters champion to "f*** off" during a feisty exchange. The Northern Irishman is preparing for the defence of the Green Jacket he won in such memorable and emotional fashion 12 months ago.

‌



McIlroy's epic extra-hole victory over Justin Rose saw him finally complete golf's Grand Slam after 11 agonising years of trying. It also led sports writer Alan Shipnuck to write a biography of the 36-year-old and his journey to golfing immortality.

‌



The book - Rory: The Heartache and Triumph of Golf's Most Human Superstar - isn't released until this week, but it didn't go down well with McIlroy, who was not been involved in the project.

‌



Shipnuck has revealed he was on the receiving end of a tirade during last year's US Open. He told the Irish Times he heard someone say "hey Alan" while chatting to McIlroy's manager, Sean O'Flaherty.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Shipnuck, who published a biography about Phil Mickelson in 2022, said: "I looked up and McIlroy was staring me down. His eyes were slits and his face twisted into a scowl.

‌



Rory McIlroy's comment to Scottie Scheffler brought up with stark difference in behaviour READ MORE :

"As soon as we made eye contact, he growled, 'f*** off.' McIlroy took a couple of steps toward us and pointed his driver at me, 'Seriously, f*** off.'"

Shipnuck asked McIlroy why he was "so bothered" by the book. He is said to have replied: "You f***ed Phil, I'm not going to make the same mistake. It p***** me off that you're making money off my name."

Despite that exchange, Shipnuck pressed ahead with the book, adding that "collaborative biographies skew toward the bland and sanitised."

‌



View 3 Images McIlroy wasn't happy with how Phil Mickelson was portrayed in a book written by Alan Shipnuck (Image: Getty Images)

He added: "He's been in the public eye for almost two decades. My job was to tell people things they don't know, to give a deeper understanding of this incredible journey.

"His appeal is, I think, that deep down he’s still this kid from the suburbs of Belfast who grew up in a working-class family. And he's retained that humility, that sense of wonder about how far he's travelled in his life.

‌



"Deep down he's never really changed. And, and I think that's what makes him compelling to a lot of people."

View 3 Images McIlroy begins the defence of his Green Jacket on Thursday afternoon UK time (Image: Erick W. Rasco/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images)

Despite that spicy exchange, Shipnuck insists he and McIlroy are "good" now, having presented him with a copy earlier this year. Writing on X this week, Shipnuck said: "I gave the book to Rory at Pebble so he could see it's a feel-good story and there's nothing in it to be overly worried about.

Article continues below

"Saw Rory that Sunday night and he said he'd read the Foreword - which has some of the spiciest material - and it made him laugh. We're good."

McIlroy has been grouped with Cameron Young and amateur Mason Howell for the first two rounds at Augusta. He begins his first round at 3:31pm UK time.

Sports.title: Patrick Mullins deserts last year’s Grand National winner to ride third-place horse
Sports.content:
Patrick Mullins deserts last year’s Grand National winner to ride third-place horse

In a surprise switch the amateur son of trainer Willie Mullie will not be aboard Nick Rockett, now the mount of Tom Bellamy, as he prefers Grangeclare West

View 2 Images Last year's Grand National winner Nick Rockett will be ridden by Tom Bellamy on Saturday

Patrick Mullins has deserted last year’s Randox Grand National winner to ride last year’s Grand National third. In an unexpected twist the amateur son of trainer Willie Mullins will not be aboard Nick Rockett, who defeated I Am Maximus and Grangeclare West, to complete a stable 1-2-3.

‌



Instead he has opted to partner Grangeclare West who warmed up for Aintree by winning the Bobbyjo Chase, a race Nick Rockett won 12 months ago and has produced the last two winners of the £1 million race.

‌



It is highly unusual for a big race jockey to turn his back on a horse on whom he has gained such historic success.

‌



Paul Townend, who won the race in 2024 on I Am Maximus, has stuck with him in every Grand National since, however Nick Rockett's campaign has been disrupted by training setbacks and he ran well below par when third of four on his belated comeback last month.

The beneficiary of Patrick Mullins’s decision is Tom Bellamy, the in-form British jockey who broke his Cheltenham Festival duck in March.

View 2 Images Tom Bellamy: rode his first Cheltenham Festival winner in March (Image: Michael Steele, Getty Images)

‌



The other Mullins jockey bookings are Brian Hayes for Spanish Harlem, Sean O’Keeffe for Lecky Watson and Danny Mullins for Champ Kiely. James Bowen will partner High Class Hero, Jonathan Burke (Captain Cody) and Donagh Meyler (Quai de Bourbon).

Bellamy, 31, is enjoying his best ever season with 64 wins, including Cheltenham success on White Noise in the Dawn Run Mares’ Novices’ Hurdle this year.

He has had five previous rides in the race but has yet to complete, with four having fallen and the other pulled up.

‌

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy makes exception for PGA Tour icon at record-breaking Masters Champions Dinner
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy makes exception for PGA Tour icon at record-breaking Masters Champions Dinner

Rory McIlroy clearly looks out for his guests after taking one Masters guest into serious consideration when crafting his Champions Dinner menu

View 2 Images Rory McIlroy adapted his Masters Champions Dinner so it suited one former winner in particular (Image: Benjamin Gilbert/Augusta National/Getty Images)

Masters champion Rory McIlroy showed his empathetic side with one small but meaningful gesture in his Champions Dinner menu. The titleholder created the most expensive menu on record at Augusta National, involving one dish specifically for three-time champion Gary Player.

‌



McIlroy, 36, finally got his chance to dictate the pre-tournament grub ahead of his title defence this week. And he clearly spared no expense as his sampler came out at an average cost of around £251 ($318) per head, almost three times as much as rival Scottie Scheffler's menu 12 months ago.

‌



The main portion of the meal included courses of yellowfin tuna carpaccio, wagyu filet mignon, seared salmon and sticky toffee pudding. However, his appetisers included a peach and ricotta flatbread starter that, as McIlroy explained, was made with Player in mind.

‌



That's because the South African icon is "90 per cent vegetarian" these days. Had it not been for McIlroy's concession, it would have meant the 1961, 1974 and 1978 Masters champion would have been left eating little other than breadsticks.

The Masters Champions Dinner is an annual tradition served up in the days leading up to the first major of the calendar year. As such, the reigning champion usually takes their opportunity to put some personal spin on proceedings.

‌



Rory McIlroy gesture sees Masters fans gasp during practice round at Augusta READ MORE :

McIlroy was quizzed over the lack of Irish influence present in his menu. However, he joked that it was all too intentional because he "wanted to enjoy the dinner, too."

Player is one of the most celebrated figures at Augusta and has served as one of the competition's ceremonial starters since 2012. However, that privilege doesn't necessarily extend to family, as Player's son, Wayne, is banned from the club for life.

View 2 Images Gary Player needed a slight tweak to the menu given he's now "90 per cent vegetarian" (Image: Ben Jared/PGA TOUR via Getty Images)

‌



It was back in 2021 that Player Jr interrupted the ceremonial tee shot by holding up a box of OnCore golf balls, which sponsored his dad. Wayne later revealed that some praised him for his advertising nous, but it didn't stop Augusta National informing him he was no longer welcome on their grounds.

"Well, they say there's no such thing as bad publicity," he recounted during an interview with Golf Digest in 2022. "I found out that that's not quite true.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Article continues below

"I had probably 50 texts after that, 40 of them said I'm a marketing genius, 10 were like, 'What the hell were you thinking?' It wasn't premeditated, but it was a tacky thing."

Wayne also revealed he wrote a letter to Augusta apologising for his actions and asking if he could be permitted entry in future. The club accepted his apology but politely informed Player's son that his ban would remain firmly in place.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury's family tell him to retire immediately just days before comeback
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury's family tell him to retire immediately just days before comeback

The 'Gypsy King' will make yet another boxing comeback this weekend, but several members of his family wish the Morecambe scrapper would stay retired

View Image Tyson Fury will return to the ring this weekend (Image: PA)

Tyson Fury is set to end yet another retirement this weekend, but his brother Tommy admits his family would rather he stay retired.

‌



The 'Gypsy King' announced his retirement last year after suffering back-to-back defeats to Oleksandr Usyk, but reversed his decision just months later. Fury will take on Arslanbek Makhmudov at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday night as he plans on a busy year in the ring.

‌



Fury's return has not been without drama after his father John revealed that he's no longer on talking terms with his son. The former two-time heavyweight world champion constantly had his father in his corner, until he decided to leave John out of his team before his second defeat to Usyk in December 2024.

‌



John is adamant that his son has not been the same since his three outings with Wilder, and has consistently called for him to hang the gloves up for good over the years. Just days before the 'Gypsy King's' return, his brother Tommy has now weighed in.

Watch Fury vs Makhmudov with free Netflix subscription This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. The fight will stream live on Netflix, which fans can get for free with Sky's £15 Essential TV bundle or £24 Ultimate TV bundle, the latter of which also includes HBO Max and Disney+.

The 26-year-old believes Tyson will benefit from the retirement life, as he told Bloody Elbow: “I think if you asked any one of his family do we want to see him keeping boxing the answer would have been an all around ‘no’. That’s all the way around the board because we care about his health.

‌



“Obviously you guys are fight fans you love to see him in the ring because he brings that entertainment. But we think of his health and everything like that so listen, he’s decided to keep fighting, it’s Tyson who is a fighting man who loves to do so. But I guess time will tell and I think he definitely still has it in him because he wouldn’t be getting in that ring if he knew he didn’t.”

Tyson Fury makes worrying admission days before comeback fight READ MORE :

Tyson Fury forced to address poor ticket sales for comeback fight READ MORE :

Regardless, the former Love Island star was quick to offer his official prediction for Saturday night's fight, stating: “I think it’s going to be a great fight. I think he probably could have picked an easier fight to come back against. He’s massive, he’s a man mountain with a knockout ratio and power and he’s been in some big fights before.

Article continues below

“The thing is, Tyson just needs to stay switched on this Saturday, box how he knows he can box and he’ll get the job done. If he does that, I don’t see the fight going past eight or ten rounds. If he boxes like I know he can Makhmudov is getting stopped late on.”

Like his older brother, Tommy is also preparing for a fight of his own. Fury has not fought since outpointing Kenan Hanjalic back in May, but will return to action in June, when he takes on former training partner Eddie Hall in a monumental Misfits showdown in Manchester.

Sports.title: Grand National 2026: Willie Mullins' right-hand man picks the one horse he would ride
Sports.content:
Grand National 2026: Willie Mullins' right-hand man picks the one horse he would ride

David Casey, assistant to the champion trainer, gives his views on the Mullins team for the Randox Grand National which is seeking a hat-trick of victories

View 4 Images Nick Rockett (right) held off I Am Maximus and Grangeclare West (centre) to win the Grand National (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Willie Mullins’s right-hand man has named the horse he would like to ride in the Randox Grand National. David Casey has worked as the champion trainer’s assistant since he retired from a successful career as a jockey.

‌



He was worked closely in preparing the Mullins team for a hat-trick bid on the £1 million race following wins with Nick Rockett, who led home a stable 1-2-3 last year, and I Am Maximus in 2024.

‌



Mullins, who also triumphed with Hedgehunter in 2005, needs one more victory to join Red Rum’s trainer Ginger McCain and Fred Rimell as the most successful trainers in the race’s history.

‌



Grand National 2026 runners: Final field confirmed as 34 horses set to line up at Aintree READ MORE :

Casey, speaking to BetSelect , has given his view on each of the nine Mullins runners and singled out the horse he believes has the best chance.

He said: “If I had to pick one I’d go with I Am Maximus. He’s had a bit of a stronger preparation this year than he did last time. He missed the Bobbyjo this year, but that was planned, whereas last year we hadn’t intended for him to miss it but he missed a couple of days of work. This year he goes in with a much better prep.

“He won the race in 2024 and was second in it last year, so there’s no doubting that he loves the place and I’d side with him. He carries 11st 12lbs but I don’t think weight seems to be as much of an issue know. It’s more about class now.

‌



View 4 Images David Casey: assessed the Willie Mullins Grand National team

“Nick Rockett had everything go well for him last year and Patrick Mullins gave him a great ride, but it hasn’t been his season so far. He missed his run in the John Durkan and at Christmas, but we eventually got him out at Down Royal to get him qualified for the race. It hasn’t been an ideal prep and you’d have to be a bit sceptical of his chances for that reason.”

Casey continued: “Nick Rockett and I Am Maximus we know will like the conditions because they’ve run so well on better ground there before,” said Casey. “I also think it will benefit the likes of Captain Cody, High Class Hero and Lecky Watson. It will bring them more to the fore.

‌

“They probably haven’t been able to show as much this season because the ground has been so bad in Ireland throughout the winter. I think those three in particular will really be suited by the nicer ground.

“Captain Cody is last year’s Scottish National winner and he won that one nicer ground, so the conditions will definitely suit him. High Class Hero ran a big race at Sandown on nicer ground as well, so those two are really in the same boat.

‌



View 4 Images I Am Maximus won the 2024 Grand National (Image: Getty Images)

“You can make a case for all of our nine runners this year,” he added. “Grangeclare West was third in it last year and has been running well this season. He was a very good winner of the Bobbyjo. Looking back at last year, he was actually very unlucky because he just got it wrong at the last and then stayed on into third. That brings him into the mix as one of our three classier horses.

“Champ Kiely is a Grade 1 winner. He would prefer a bit of softer ground, but he won’t struggle to travel through the race and he’s also a very good jumper. There’s a slight question mark over whether he stays, but if he does then he’ll be in the mix.

‌



View 4 Images Captain Cody, ridden by Harry Cobden, on their way to winning the Coral Scottish Grand National (Image: PA)

“Spanish Harlem is a bit in-and-out, but on his day he’s a very good horse. He won a Kerry National last September and was set to be a good winner of the Thyestes before unseating at the last. He’s another who’ll like the better ground.

“Quai De Bourbon is one who had the option of the Irish National, which we’re glad we skipped now given how Emmet’s won. He was third there last year after a tough campaign and he comes here with a lighter campaign and he showed huge improvement in his last run at Leopardstown. I think he’s capable of improving from that, and that should put him in with a chance here.”

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy reveals very awkward Masters Champions Dinner moment alongside Justin Rose
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy reveals very awkward Masters Champions Dinner moment alongside Justin Rose

Rory McIlroy has lifted the lid on a "really awkward" moment he and Justin Rose shared pulling up to the Masters before his Grand Slam moment

View 2 Images Rory McIlroy and Justin Rose shared an "awkward" moment together at Augusta National last year (Image: Harry How/Getty Images)

Masters champion Rory McIlroy can afford to walk around Augusta National with a lot more swagger now he's reached Grand Slam status. But it wasn't always so smooth, as the Northern Irishman revealed when recounting a "really awkward" moment with Justin Rose last year.

‌



Before the British duo went on to finish as the top two at the 2025 Masters, there came the small matter of knowing where to park. Previous champions at Augusta National get certain privileges, after all, a premium parking spot next to the clubhouse being one of them.

‌



So it made for a "weird" crossroads moment when Ryder Cup team-mates McIlroy and Rose pulled up to the venue. Speaking ahead of this year's tournament, the former described his relief at not having to worry about such frivolous matters anymore.

‌



"It was weird," he told reporters this week while describing last year's incident. "I was pulling up Magnolia Lane, and you get to the [Founders Circle], and I’m like, 'Well, do I go and park way over at the parking lot?' Because I’m not going to park in the champions parking lot.

"Then at that specific moment, the champions were having their cocktails out on the balcony. I’m like, 'I don’t want to valet, get out, they’re going to see me and it’s going to be weird'.

Rory McIlroy gesture sees Masters fans gasp during practice round at Augusta READ MORE :

"So I had this really awkward moment with it all last year. Yeah, thankfully that was the last time that I needed to do that."

‌



McIlroy and Rose took part in an iconic play-off battle at the conclusion of the 2025 Masters. It briefly looked as though Englishman Rose would pull off the upset and win his first major in 12 years, only for McIlroy to end his own 11-year search and finally complete the career Grand Slam.

View 2 Images McIlroy's return to Augusta as reigning champion comes with a lot more perks (Image: Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



He returned to Augusta this year as the proud owner of his own iconic Green Jacket. Among the other perks of being a Masters winner is the opportunity to design one's own Masters Dinner.

After a range of appetisers, McIlroy served his fellow champions a yellowfin tuna carpaccio starter, followed by a main choice of either wagyu filet mignon or seared salmon. To finish, he chose a dessert of sticky toffee pudding with vanilla ice cream and described the enjoyment he had piecing the meal together.

"It was a fun process to go through," said McIlroy. "I was trying to achieve something that I would enjoy but also something that ties back to experiences that I’ve had, but also wanted it to be something that all the other people in that room would enjoy as well.

Article continues below

"People keep asking me, ‘Why didn’t you go more Irish?’ And I said, 'Because I want to enjoy the dinner as well'."

Sports.title: Tyson Fury forced to address poor ticket sales for comeback fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury forced to address poor ticket sales for comeback fight

The former two-time heavyweight world champion will return to the ring this weekend, but it seems his comeback as not peaked nation's fans' interest

View Image Tyson Fury has provided an update on ticket sales ahead of his boxing return (Image: ITV)

Tyson Fury is adamant Tottenham Hotspur Stadium will be a sell-out amid concerns of ticket sales ahead of his comeback fight.

‌



The former two-time heavyweight champion will end his fifth retirement from boxing on Saturday night when he takes on bear-wrestling heavyweight Arslanbek Makhmudov.

‌



Saturday night's showdown will be streamed live on Netflix to its 300million customers worldwide. As a bonus to fight fans, there is no charge for existing subscribers. Many fans are seemingly happier to watch the event from the comforts of their own home, rather than heading to north London.

‌



As a result, there are still plenty of tickets on sale now - despite the fact general on sale kicked off months ago. Ticket-selling prices such as Viagogo are still selling seats in the majority of blocks, while on Ticketmaster recently, seats could be seen priced at a staggeringly low fee of £4.95.

Amid fears there could be plenty of empty seats on Saturday night, Fury has provided a major update and insists the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium will in fact be sold out on fight night. "It's been a... let's just say it's been a very busy few months with the boxing scene all around the world," he told Good Morning Britain.
